newsitem.title: USA: Maryland cuts income tax, boosts school spending.
newsitem.headline: Maryland cuts income tax, boosts school spending.

text.p: Maryland's General Assembly has adopted a $15.4 billion budget that cuts income taxes by 10 percent over five years and steers more money to Baltimore schools.
In a 90-day session that ended late Monday night, lawmakers approved a bill that allocates an extra $421 million for public schools over five years.

Despite objections from county school officials and suburban lawmakers, the plan divides $167 million of school funding among Maryland's 23 counties and gives Baltimore schools the remaining $254 million.

It also increases state authority over Baltimore schools, giving the governor, state Board of Education and Baltimore mayor shared authority to appoint a 10-member school board. Currently Baltimore Mayor Kurt Schmoke appoints the entire board.
The budget includes $415 million of capital projects, including $124.5 million for public school construction, $115.7 million for higher education and $28.5 million for prison building.

Lawmakers approved Gov. Parris Glendening's proposal to restrict growth in rural areas concentrating state spending for roads and utilities to areas that are already densely populated. But they rejected the governor's proposal to double the state's 36-cents-a-pack tax on cigarettes.
Lawmakers also killed proposals to approve casino gambling and slot machines, which Glendening had said he would veto.
